req.title: Basic-auth handles special characters
req.statement: The system shall URL-decode <user> and <passwd> path segments before comparing against the supplied Basic credentials.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states that /basic-auth/<user>/<passwd> must URL-decode path segments before comparing against Basic credentials. Tests must cover: (1) positive - URL-encoded special chars in both user and passwd that decode correctly and match supplied credentials; (2) negative - credentials that do NOT match the URL-decoded path values return 401; (3) boundary - single special character at the boundary of URL encoding (e.g., space encoded as %20, plus sign, at-sign). We also test that the response JSON payload is exactly {authenticated: true, user: <decoded_user>} and that the 401 path returns exactly 401. The check_basic_auth function compares auth.username == user and auth.password == passwd where user/passwd are the Flask route parameters (which Werkzeug URL-decodes from the path). We drive the Flask test client in-process.

tests.name: test_basic_auth_special_chars_positive_url_encoded_user_and_passwd
preconditions: httpbin Flask app is importable in-process
Client sends correct Basic credentials matching URL-decoded path segments
actions: Construct GET /basic-auth/user%40example/p%40ss with Authorization: Basic base64(user@example:p@ss)
trace: R-HTTPBIN-041: URL-decode path segments before comparing credentials
EP: valid credentials with @ special character
tests.executable:
import base64
from httpbin.core import app

client = app.test_client()

user = 'user@example'
passwd = 'p@ss'
creds = base64.b64encode(f'{user}:{passwd}'.encode()).decode()
headers = {'Authorization': f'Basic {creds}'}

r = client.get('/basic-auth/user%40example/p%40ss', headers=headers)
assert r.status_code == 200
data = r.get_json()
assert data['authenticated'] == True
assert data['user'] == 'user@example'
